4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable “gta 5 (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)” experience in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them upon completion.
- Support phone/tablet play with responsive touch controls.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created an original arcade-style open-city driving game, “Neon Coast,” rather than reproducing GTA V assets.
- Built a Three.js city-driving experience with delivery missions, traffic, pickups, heat, vehicle damage, HUD, keyboard controls, and touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI, styling, Three.js gameplay, missions, mobile controls, minimap, and driving HUD.
- Started local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Verified the browser loads the game; created and inspected `screenshots/neon-coast.jpg` at 1280×800.
- Adjusted initial pause overlay visibility, building placement, and minimap draw timing.

### Active
- Validate recent changes to city/building placement and complete a gameplay smoke test, including starting a run and checking touch controls.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload the page and inspect the latest `screenshots/neon-coast.jpg`.
2. Smoke-test starting the game, driving, and mission/drop completion; resolve any runtime or visual issues.
3. Report the completed game and the original-game assumption briefly.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and HUD elements.
- `style.css`: Responsive desktop/mobile layout and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, city, vehicle physics, missions, input, and HUD.
- `screenshots/neon-coast.jpg`: Latest visual check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser console showed one missing `favicon.ico` 404 and WebGL readback performance warnings; no game-script errors were reported.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-city driving game for phone and tablet in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- Support responsive touch controls for phone and tablet play.
- Save small JPEG screenshots at viewport widths no greater than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built an original arcade-style open-city game, “Neon Coast,” rather than reproducing GTA V assets.
- Included delivery missions, traffic, pickups, heat, vehicle damage, HUD, keyboard controls, and touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game interface, responsive styling, Three.js city and driving, missions, minimap, HUD, and touch controls.
- Started the local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Smoke-tested starting a run, keyboard driving, and touch acceleration; touch driving reached 47 km/h.
- Tested mission completion: driving to the first drop displayed completion and increased cash from `$2,450` to `$2,700`.
- Added `favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html`; latest browser console check had no errors or warnings.

### Active
- Capture and inspect a fresh screenshot after the latest favicon change, then report completion.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Capture a fresh JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only that latest image.
2. Briefly report the completed game and note the original-game assumption.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and HUD.
- `style.css`: Responsive desktop/mobile layout and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, city, vehicle physics, missions, input, and HUD.
- `favicon.svg`: Game favicon.
- `screenshots/neon-coast.jpg`: Existing visual check; recapture after the latest changes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The game runs at `http://localhost:3002`; browser smoke tests confirmed driving and first-drop completion.
- Earlier browser output reported WebGL readback performance warnings; no game-script errors were observed.
